# A column drop's header scroll clamp resets the grid's horizontal scroll

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderCellRectSync.spec.mjs` "repeated back-and-forth drag keeps every header rect locked to its cell rect" flakes `e2e-engine (3/4)` (`#19967`, job 119372987209). Locally the real arm failed 5/96 under 6 workers; a probe replaying it failed 3/144.

- **Always pass 2:** in every failing trace, pass 1 drags and drops normally, and pass 2's press never arms. The traces' pointer coordinates show why: pass 1 pressed the dragged header at x=1724, pass 2 at x=2136 / 2081, outside the 1920 px viewport. After pass 1's drop the grid had lost its 412 px horizontal scroll.
- **The mechanism, from the arm's own scroll trace:** one header-toolbar scroll event fires 36–69 ms after the release, with the toolbar at 0 while the body's `--grid-scroll-left` still reads 412. At the failure, toolbar, body var and scrollbar all read 0.

## The Problem

The drop's layout restore clamps the header toolbar's native `scrollLeft` to 0 for a moment. That is known: `processDragEnd()`'s own comment in `src/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` describes it and re-applies the scroll truth afterwards. Since `#19957` (`#19955`), `GridHorizontalScrollSync#onHeaderScroll` routes every native header scroll that is not its own echo into the scrollbar. So when the clamp's scroll event lands, the clamped 0 becomes the grid's scroll truth. The scrollbar, body and `owner.scrollLeft` follow it, and the re-apply then has nothing left to restore.

User-visible: reorder a column while the grid is scrolled right, and the grid can jump back to its left edge. Before `#19957`, the same late clamp offset the header alone, which is the bug class this arm was written for, and the re-apply hid it unless the clamp landed after it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/GridHorizontalScrollSync.mjs` `onHeaderScroll()` copies the header's `scrollLeft` into the scrollbar whenever it differs from `registration.headerScrollLeft`. It does not ask whether the header could hold the scrollbar's position at all.
- `SortZone#processDragEnd()` re-applies `owner.scrollLeft` to the toolbar after `await me.timeout(30)`, when `owner.scrollLeft > 0`. The toolbar's own restore update (`owner.updateDepth = 2; owner.update()`) is not awaited, so under load it can land after the re-apply.
- **Design authority:** that comment ("restoring the items out of `position: absolute` passes through a reflow frame where the owner toolbar has no scrollable overflow, so the browser clamps the toolbar element's native scrollLeft to 0 … Re-apply the worker-side scroll truth to the toolbar element once the restore has settled"), and `#19955`'s intent: a header scrolled into view by focus moves the grid. Neither intends a layout clamp to move the grid.

## The Fix

1. `onHeaderScroll()` routes a header scroll only while the header can hold the scrollbar's position, `scrollerNode.scrollLeft <= headerNode.scrollWidth - headerNode.clientWidth + 1`. A header that cannot reach it was clamped by layout, not scrolled.
2. `processDragEnd()` re-applies the truth once the toolbar's pending updates have landed (`await owner.promiseUpdate()`) instead of after a fixed 30 ms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A header that loses its scrollable overflow for a moment does not move the grid: the scrollbar keeps its position. A header scrolled by focus still moves the grid (`#19955`'s arm stays green).
- [ ] AC-2: After a column drop while scrolled, the grid keeps its horizontal scroll position and the header sits back on it.
- [ ] AC-3: A deterministic browser arm for AC-1 is red on base and green at head.
- [ ] AC-4: Under the probe's load (6 workers), `HeaderCellRectSync.spec.mjs`'s arm passes every run at head (144 runs). This is an outside-CI receipt.

## Out of Scope

- Why the restore clamps at all. Keeping the drag's extent sentinel until the items are back in flow could remove the clamp at its source; that needs its own measurement.
